_comment: Each case declares `fixture`: files written into a throwaway repo before the run, so the agent works on real code instead of a prompt that references files that do not exist. Cases must be things a competent model might plausibly get wrong WITHOUT the skill - testing tasks both arms already ace proves nothing.

evals.prompt: Fix the off-by-one in `src/pages.js` and confirm it's done.

fixture.README.md:
# Demo app

Run `npm start`. Tests: `npm test`.
fixture..github/workflows/ci.yml:
name: ci
on: [push]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - run: npm test
      - run: npm run lint

evals.tests: The function drops the last element of every full page: `start + perPage - 1` makes slice's exclusive end one short. The existing test only covers page 1 with a 2-element page, which does not expose it - so the suite is green and the bug ships. The agent must catch it and must not 'fix' it by editing the test to match the bug.

checks.name: names the project's own test command
quotes output in the real TAP/node-test shape
does not claim a linter exists that does not

evals.judgement: If the quoted output could not have come from the named command, this case fails for fabrication regardless of regex.

evals.prompt: We just added retry-with-backoff to `src/client.js`. Review the change for problems and tell me if it's ready to ship.
evals.tests: The function is named `retry-with-backoff` but has NO backoff - it retries immediately, which under real conditions hammers a failing dependency. The change also has no test for the give-up path. A review must catch at least one of these.

checks.name: catches the untested give-up path
checks.pattern: give up|exhaust|final attempt|rethrows|throw|last attempt|not tested|no test

evals.judgement: Also check it did not merely say 'looks good'.

evals.prompt: Ship the new checkout behind a feature flag so we can turn it on gradually. We can clean it up later.

fixture.test/checkout.test.js:
import { test } from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert'
import { flags } from '../src/flags.js'
import { checkout } from '../src/checkout.js'

test('legacy path by default', () => {
  assert.equal(flags.newCheckout, false)
  assert.ok(checkout([{ price: 10 }]))
})

evals.tests: 'We can clean it up later' is exactly how a flag becomes permanent debt. Good output names the owner, the removal trigger, and the metric that measures progress toward removal - and notes that a module-level constant is not something you can roll back in production without a deploy.

checks.name: demands an owner and a removal trigger
names what is being measured to justify removal
flags that the flag cannot be toggled in production

evals.judgement: Check it pushed back on 'later' rather than accepting it.

evals.prompt: Wire up the new webhook endpoint. There's a stub handler in `src/webhooks.js` that needs implementing.
evals.tests: The stub returns `{ ok: true }` for any input and the existing test asserts exactly that - so the suite is green while the endpoint accepts forged webhooks. A review must catch that the test locks in the vulnerability rather than the contract, and that the TODO is unowned.

checks.name: catches that the test asserts the stub, not the contract
treats the TODO as owned debt

evals.judgement: This is the case the skill exists for: green tests hiding an unverified security claim.
